course_name_original: Fundamentals of Machining, Metrology and Product Design
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Machining, Metrology and Product Design

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic methods of the machining and a quiddity of the cutting process.

syllabus_topics: Basic production technologies, development of machining technologies and their division, basic concepts
Geometry of cutting tools - tool planes
Tool materials, coatings, overview, properties, use, correct tool selection, calculation of tool costs
Machining of rotating surfaces, achieved quality parameters - turning
Machining of flat and shaped surfaces, achieved quality parameters - milling
Clamping of tools and workpieces during turning and milling
Tool wear, causes of tool wear, course of wear, Taylor's relation, prediction of wear
Machining temperature, heat dissipation and heat balance, machining forces, chip formation, selection and optimization of cutting conditions
Machining of holes - drilling, boring, reaming, boring, shaping, broaching, machines and tools, clamping, material cutting
Finishing rotating surfaces, grinding and other technologies to achieve the highest quality and accuracy of surfaces
Finishing non-rotating surfaces, grinding and other technologies to achieve the highest quality and accuracy of surfaces
Achieved dimensional accuracy and surface quality of basic production technologies, basic means for quality control
Technological procedure, economics of machining process, optimization procedures, selection of suitable technology
Induction course, organization of laboratory works, safety standards, basic terminology of machining process.
Basic terminology of machining process - laboratory practice.
Basic terminology of machining process - cutting tools.
Real shop practice.
Real shop practice.
Real shop practice.
Credit test, submission of specifications, credit.
bibliography: Boothroyd, G., Knight, W. A. Fundamentals of Machining and Machine Tools. Marcel Dekker, Inc., New York and Basel, 1989
